text.p: Sherwin-Williams Co said its stock regained 2-7/8 to 54-7/8 Tuesday after a $4 decline Monday when the market learned of some business lost.
"It has rebounded to almost where it was," spokeswoman Lydia Bazarko said in a telephone interview. "It is now trading in the range of the past several weeks."

She said Monday's decline came after the market learned that Home Depot Inc will no longer carry Dutch Boy paints nor private label paints made by Sherwin-Williams. For 1997, on an annualized basis, the business amounts to about $60 million, she said.

She said analysts estimate the Cleveland-based paint firm's overall 1997 sales will be about $4.7 billion after it completes its previously announced acquisition of Thompson Minwax Holding Corp, which makes wood stains and varnishes, or about $4.4 billion excluding Thompson Minwax.

McDonald & Co analyst Justin Maurer said Sherwin-Williams declined to cut prices for Home Depot. He said the lost business amounts to about one percent of overall sales which he expects to be easily offset, and he will not alter his 1997 earnings estimate of $3.00 a share. Maurer estimated the company will earn $2.65 a share for 1996 versus $2.34 in 1995.
